faq_heading: Sardis West Vedder: your questions answered

blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. This section was written from City of Chilliwack, School District 33, BC Transit and Chilliwack Museum pages, and replaces text that was repeated on the other Sardis guides.
How the Evans and Unsworth corridors came to be

Sardis sits on the traditional, unceded territory of the Stó:lō people. The City’s Sardis Neighbourhood Plan says the Ts’elxwéyeqw Tribe has lived here for thousands of years, and that mid-19th-century settlers came to farm, mostly dairy and hops.

Unsworth Road has the longer paper trail. The City's Trail Network Plan says the old New Westminster to Yale wagon road turned north after crossing Vedder Creek and ran along what is now Unsworth Road before reaching the small settlement then called Centerville. The Chilliwack Museum records that A.C. Wells settled a farm in Sardis in 1865, and that five generations of the Evans family have lived on a farm off Yale Road West, where a log cabin thought to date from the early 1860s still stands.

blocks.text: Getting around: Vedder Road is the spine

The Sardis plan calls Vedder Road the north-south spine of Sardis and says a frequent bus line with 15-minute service runs along it to downtown and the Canada Education Park. BC Transit's current Rider's Guide lists route 51 Vedder and route 66 FVX at the Vedder Road and Luckakuck Way stop. Route 52 Evans has separate weekday, Saturday, and Sunday and holiday timetables, with timing points at Cottonwood Mall, Evans Road at Yale Road, Ashwell Road at Hodgins Avenue and downtown. The guide gives no frequency for route 52, so read the weekday timetable before you count on it for a commute.

Two changes are on the City’s list: a Vedder Road corridor plan with wider sidewalks, street trees and better crossings, and a transit exchange next to Luckakuck Way. The Trail Network Plan also proposes a rail trail linking Sardis, Yarrow and Greendale with downtown. None is built yet, so treat them as direction, not a promise.

Evans Elementary is at 7600 Evans Road (604-858-3057) and Unsworth Elementary is at 5685 Unsworth Road (604-858-4510). School District 33 sets catchments by address, so check the exact home with its school locator before you write an offer.

I could not confirm a City park inside the sub-area, because the City does not map parks to MLS names. The Sardis plan lists Sardis Park, Sardis Sports Fields, Wells Landing Park, Manuel Park and Roy Park as existing Sardis parks.

blocks.text: What the plan means for buyers and owners

The plan says no vacant greenfield land is left in Sardis, so growth will come from infill and redevelopment, bounded by Highway 1, the ALR and the Vedder neighbourhood. It estimates Sardis will need roughly 1,300 to 1,700 more attached homes and 1,100 to 1,700 apartment units by 2041. Urban residential land allows houses, duplexes and accessory dwellings up to 10 m high; townhouses belong within about a ten-minute walk of services, and apartments of up to six storeys near frequent transit.

For a larger or combined lot, the plan expects redevelopment at higher density, and for a standard lot a split into two smaller lots. Along Evans Road the picture is different: the plan describes West Evans as ALR land between Stevenson and Evans roads, and says changing the urban boundary there would take talks with the Agricultural Land Commission. The City's small-scale housing guide (updated September 2024) allows up to three or four units on eligible lots. They must be inside the urban growth boundary, under 4,050 square metres, on City water and sewer, and in a listed zone. A secondary suite is allowed in any single detached home, needs a building permit, and cannot sit below the flood construction level.
Before you pay for a lot on the strength of what a neighbour built, ask Planning (604-793-2906) for its zone and plan designation.
Water and flood questions to ask

The City's drinking water comes from the Sardis-Vedder Aquifer, which lies north of the Vedder River and reaches up to Highway 1. The City says the water table is 5 to 10 metres down, the soil above it is coarse and very permeable, and its wells draw from 30 to 40 metres. So spills on the surface can reach it quickly. If the home has an old oil tank or a private well, ask about both.

Flooding is different by lot. The City says Vedder River floods are mostly fall and winter events that last 1 to 2 days, and that provincial dyke standards use a 1-in-200-year flood. Bylaw 4519 sets setbacks of 75 m from the Vedder River and 30 m from the Vedder Canal and Chilliwack River. The plan adds that the northern part of Sardis lies in the Fraser River floodplain, where buildings must be floodproofed. Call the Flood Information Line at 604-793-2757 with the exact address before you rely on a general map.

faq.q: Where is Sardis West Vedder, and is there an official boundary?
faq.a: It is an MLS sub-area name, and the City publishes no boundary for it. The nearest official maps are the Sardis Neighbourhood Plan and the South Vedder Neighbourhood Plan, whose western edge is Vedder Road. Send me an address and I will check.

faq.q: Which elementary schools are in Sardis West Vedder?
faq.a: Evans Elementary at 7600 Evans Road and Unsworth Elementary at 5685 Unsworth Road. Catchments are set by address, so confirm with the School District 33 school locator.

faq.q: Is there a bus on Evans Road?
faq.a: BC Transit’s route 52 Evans has weekday, Saturday, and Sunday and holiday timetables, with timing points at Cottonwood Mall, Evans Road at Yale Road, Ashwell Road at Hodgins Avenue and downtown. The Rider’s Guide gives no frequency, so check the timetable for your hours.

faq.q: Can I add a suite or build more than one home on my lot?
faq.a: A secondary suite is allowed in any single detached house, with a building permit. Up to three or four units are possible on eligible lots under the City’s small-scale housing rules: inside the urban growth boundary, on City water and sewer, under 4,050 square metres and in a listed zone. Ask Planning about the exact lot.

faq.q: What are the Vedder River floods like?
faq.a: The City says the larger floods happen in fall and winter, usually last 1 to 2 days, and give little warning. It keeps a yearly-reviewed flood response plan for the Vedder. Flood construction levels and setbacks come from the Floodplain Regulation Bylaw, and apply lot by lot.

faq.q: Is any of Sardis West Vedder farmland?
faq.a: The Agricultural Land Reserve is set parcel by parcel. The Sardis plan treats the land between Stevenson Road and Evans Road as ALR. Look up any larger lot on the Agricultural Land Commission map before you plan to build or subdivide.
